verdict.rationale: Undermind is built for scholarly literature search. Its docs describe searching the global literature and a paper's references and citations, with filters by author, journal and year, plus resolving DOIs and reading full-text PDFs. Several independent users report it surfaced relevant papers they had missed in Google Scholar, arXiv, ScienceDirect and PubMed. Missing for 10: documentation of which corpora and sources are indexed, and coverage of gray literature and dissertations, which hands-on users said was thin.

support.subject: As a researcher, I can search scholarly literature and primary sources, not just the open web

citations.quote: Searches the global literature, papers already in the workspace, or a paper’s references and citations in seconds. Filters by author, journal, year, and PDF availability.
Resolve titles, DOIs, or an entire bibliography into matching papers in bulk.
Fetches open-access PDFs automatically; paywalled PDFs can be read after workspace upload.
Pretty good: it found some useful references the user had missed in Google Scholar and arXiv.
